Age waivers are not granted, so candidates must plan their application timeline carefully.

sections.content:
The United States Air Force Academy (USAFA) in Colorado Springs trains cadets to become officers in the US Air Force and Space Force. The four-year program combines a bachelor's degree, military training, athletics and leadership development, and graduates are commissioned as second lieutenants.

Tuition, room and board are fully paid, and cadets receive a monthly stipend. In return, graduates owe at least five years of active-duty service, or ten years for pilots. The Class of 2029 brought in 1,112 appointees, with an average GPA of 3.86.
sections.title: What the Air Force Academy is

sections.content:
Applicants must be US citizens aged 17 to 23 on July 1 of the entry year, unmarried, with no dependents, and in good physical and medical condition. Nearly every applicant also needs a nomination, most commonly from a US Representative, a US Senator or the Vice President.

A nomination is only an endorsement, not an offer of admission. Candidates should apply for every nomination category they qualify for, because the Academy's admissions board makes the final appointment decision independently.
sections.title: Eligibility and the nomination

sections.content:
The Academy judges candidates on a whole-person score built from academics, leadership, athletics and the selection panel's review. The Class of 2029 averaged a 3.86 GPA, and competitive SAT or ACT scores matter: the SAT is required for international candidates, with math scores below 580 considered uncompetitive.

Leadership in school, sports or community service strengthens the file. Applicants file a pre-candidate questionnaire, usually by December 31, and submit official test scores by January 31 of the entry year.
sections.title: Academics, SAT/ACT and the whole-person score

sections.content:
Every candidate must pass the Candidate Fitness Assessment (CFA), which tests running, push-ups, sit-ups, pull-ups and other physical tasks. The DoDMERB medical examination checks cardiovascular health, vision, hearing and overall fitness for military service.

Cadets who fail the CFA or the medical review cannot be appointed, even with strong academics. Training for the CFA should start months before the test date, with regular running, strength work and practice of each event under timed conditions.
